hints: Focus on electrons here, this is a redox reaction so the electrons lost must exactly equal the electrons gained.
Notice that $\text{M}^{2+}$ to $\text{M}^{4+}$ loses 2 electrons, while each Cr in dichromate goes from +6 to +3.
Work out the total electron gain for $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ to $2\text{Cr}^{3+}$ and ask how many $\text{M}^{2+}$ ions are needed to supply that many electrons.
walkthrough:
**Write the two half-equations**

Think of this as electrons being passed from one ion to the other. M is oxidised and chromium is reduced.

Oxidation: $$\text{M}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{M}^{4+} + 2e^-$$

**Count electrons gained by dichromate**

In $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$, each Cr is +6. In $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, each Cr is +3. So each Cr gains 3 electrons.

Reduction: $$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Balance electrons lost and gained**

We gain 6 electrons but each $\text{M}^{2+}$ only gives 2 electrons. To balance, we need 3 lots of the oxidation step.
$$3 \times (\text{M}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{M}^{4+} + 2e^-) = 3\text{M}^{2+} \rightarrow 3\text{M}^{4+} + 6e^-$$

**Combine to get the full equation**

Add the 6-electron reduction to the 6-electron oxidation and cancel the electrons.
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 3\text{M}^{2+} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{M}^{4+}$$

options.A: Incorrect. One $\text{M}^{2+}$ only supplies 2 electrons, but dichromate needs 6 electrons. Charge is also not balanced (+14 on left, +10 on right).
options.B: Incorrect. Two $\text{M}^{2+}$ ions supply only 4 electrons, but 6 electrons are needed to reduce $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ to $2\text{Cr}^{3+}$. This is a common slip if you forget there are 2 Cr atoms.
options.C: Correct. Three $\text{M}^{2+}$ ions lose 3 x 2 = 6 electrons, exactly matching the 6 electrons gained when $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ forms $2\text{Cr}^{3+}$. Atoms and charge (+18 on both sides) both balance.
options.D: Incorrect. Six $\text{M}^{2+}$ ions would supply 12 electrons, double what is needed. This trap comes from confusing the 6 electrons needed with needing 6 metal ions.
